decision.text: On point estimates, only Atlas-M and Brisk-S, each with high reasoning and one retry, clear the pass-rate gate in all four tasks. Both overrun the latency budget over all cases, and Atlas-M costs {cost_per_month.atlas-m.high.r1} a month against Brisk-S's {cost_per_month.brisk-s.high.r1}.

Reasoning effort buys the pass rate and spends the latency budget: every configuration inside the budget overall misses the pass-rate gate in at least one task, and the latency gate itself has no figure in any task.

Brisk-S high reasoning with retry clears each task by a point and a half or less. Reading each task as holding its traffic share of cases, a run of today's size would read it below the line on multi-hop {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.task.multihop.wrong_side} of the time, on ambiguous entity {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.task.disamb.wrong_side} and on date math {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.task.datemath.wrong_side}.

Brisk-S low reasoning with retry sits exactly on the line in date math, so a run reads it either side {assumed.share.settle.criteria.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.task.datemath.wrong_side} of the time; the routed mix in the next steps leans on this leg and on the three thin legs above.

Scores:
- 1. First screen: 1 of 2. The headline, lede and decision block say clearly that nothing is shown to clear both gates. They also say why: only Atlas-M and Brisk-S with high reasoning and retry clear the pass-rate gate in every task, and both run over the latency budget across all cases (2551 ms and 870 ms against 600 ms). This also covers the computed fact about Atlas-M high with retry. But the lede says per-task latency is what could change the answer, and that leaves out a second risk of similar size. - 2. Coherent story: 2 of 2. c1 (who clears the pass-rate gate), c2 (who stays inside the latency budget), c3 (the nearest miss inside the budget), c4 (why it misses) and c5 (the levers) build one story, and the no-call matches the dominance check: no option survives, and both high-reasoning-with-retry setups are undecided on latency. The confidence line still says High. c5's 'by less as reasoning rises' states a trend that its own block does not support: all three interactions (-1.7, -2.2, -0.5) have intervals that cross zero, and the caption admits none is separated. The weak axis of Brisk-S high with retry, its tail latency of 870 ms, is shown plainly.

Method explains why a tail over the budget across all cases means some task is over it too, as long as the tasks split the cases.

Brisk-S high with retry is just as thin on ambiguous entity (+0.6, reads below the line 29.9% of the time) and date math (+0.9, 16.5%).
